Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D concentrations were significantly correlated with depressive symptom scores on the PHQ-9.
Sentence: "Vitamin D concentrations were significantly correlated with PHQ-9 and HAMD-17 scale scores."
Measured as: PHQ-9 score
Population: 425 patients with depression
Intervention: Serum vitamin D concentration (measured, not given)
Comparator: None; correlation across participants
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 425
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both bear on vitamin D and depressive symptoms, but they differ in design, population, exposure and measure, so they conflict genuinely, with the design contrast (cross-sectional correlation vs single-arm uncontrolled case series) as the deciding difference.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","outcome_measure","comparator"],"detail":"design: cross-sectional correlation of serum level (n = 425) vs uncontrolled single-arm case series of a vitamin D3/folic acid/B12 combination in Parkinson's patients"}
